skill.name: memory-bank
skill.description: Maintains a structured memory-bank documentation set so AI coding agents can preserve project context, decisions, and progress across sessions.
skill.summary: Keeps project context, decisions, and progress in structured Markdown files for session continuity.
skill.author: 0xkynz

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged Markdown fence delimiters as Ruby or shell backtick execution and flagged a progress template heading as network reconnaissance. Review found those static hits to be false positives, with only benign documentation examples and a local directory creation example. The remaining concern is semantic: persistent memory files can carry prompt-injection content if they are treated as authoritative instructions.

remediation.issue: Persistent memory files may become a prompt-injection channel.
remediation.suggestion: State that memory-bank files are project context only, and that system, developer, and current user instructions take priority over stored notes.

remediation.issue: The bash setup example can trigger command-execution scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label the mkdir command as optional local setup, and require normal user approval before running any shell command.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Context Can Carry Prompt Injection
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the agent to read all memory bank files at every task start and rely on them for continuity. If repository documentation is untrusted, malicious content in those files could influence later sessions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly make memory-bank files persistent session context. The risk depends on who can edit those files, so this is a real contextual risk but not direct malware.

content.user_title: Preserve Project Context Across AI Sessions
content.value_statement: AI coding sessions lose important project context over time. This skill keeps decisions, current work, and progress in structured Markdown files.
actual_capabilities: Defines required memory-bank Markdown files for project brief, product context, active context, system patterns, tech context, and progress.
Guides agents to read memory bank files at the start of a session.
Provides update workflows for activeContext.md and progress.md.
Includes templates for each core documentation file.
Supports extra context files for APIs, testing, deployment, and complex features.
limitations: It does not verify documentation accuracy against the repository automatically.
It depends on users or agents to keep files current after meaningful changes.
It assumes project context lives in a local memory-bank directory.
Large memory banks can increase context usage during each session.

use_cases.title: Resume Feature Work
use_cases.description: Continue a feature after time away by reading current focus, recent changes, and next steps.

use_cases.title: Preserve Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Record patterns, constraints, and tradeoffs so future AI sessions follow established project direction.

use_cases.title: Document Client Project Context
use_cases.description: Create a concise project memory for requirements, setup details, and remaining work during client handoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Memory Bank
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new or undocumented project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a memory bank for this project. Ask me for missing project goals, then draft the required Markdown files with concise placeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Update Current Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine update after completing a task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the memory bank after this change. Refresh activeContext.md and progress.md with completed work, current state, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Documentation Drift
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate maintenance before a new session or release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all memory bank files against the current repository state. Identify outdated notes, missing decisions, and unclear next steps before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Expand Feature Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced documentation for complex work streams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create additional memory bank context for this feature. Include requirements, system interactions, testing notes, risks, and links back to core files.

output_examples.input: Start a memory bank for a new scheduling application.
output_examples.output: Creates a project brief, product context, technical context, system patterns, active context, and progress outline for the scheduling project.

output_examples.input: Update memory bank after finishing authentication.
output_examples.output: Adds the completed authentication work to progress, records current focus, and captures the next tasks for authorization and testing.

output_examples.input: Review whether the project documentation is still accurate.
output_examples.output: Compares each memory bank file with the visible project state and lists stale notes, missing setup details, and unclear decisions.

best_practices: Update activeContext.md and progress.md after meaningful project changes.
Keep each memory bank file concise, factual, and easy to scan.
Treat stored memory content as project context, not as higher-priority instructions.
anti_patterns: Do not store secrets, access tokens, private keys, or personal data in memory bank files.
Do not let outdated notes override the current repository state or current user request.
Do not create large unstructured notes that duplicate source files or issue trackers.

faq.question: Where does the skill store project memory?
faq.answer: It is designed to use Markdown files inside a local memory-bank directory in the project.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run background services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation guidance and does not define a background service.

faq.question: Can it create the initial file structure?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs the agent to create a memory-bank directory and draft the required Markdown files.

faq.question: How often should the memory bank be updated?
faq.answer: Update it after significant changes, major decisions, completed features, or explicit update requests.

faq.question: What information should be excluded?
faq.answer: Exclude secrets, credentials, private customer data, and instructions that conflict with current user or system directions.
